// cmd/foundry/supervisor.go
func newSupervisorCmd() *cobra.Command {
    var dashboard bool
    // ...
    cmd.Flags().BoolVar(&dashboard, "dashboard", false, "Run with TUI dashboard")
    
    RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {

        }

func runSupervisorWithDashboard(ctx context.Context, cfg supervisorConfig) error {
    // Create shared state channel

        runCycleWithSnapshot(cfg, state, stateCh)
    }()

title: Fix: Disk at 99% - implement worker log rotation
description:
## Summary
Disk is at 99% (13G free on 927G). Worker logs in ~/.forge/logs/workers/ have grown to 1.4GB unbounded. Tmux pipe-pane uses `tee -a` which appends indefinitely with no size checks. The `RotatingWriter` from forge-2gr exists in `internal/logs/logs.go` but cannot be used with tmux pipe-pane (it is a Go io.Writer, while tmux owns the file handle). Need pre-start rotation and automatic cleanup.

**Note**: This task supersedes forge-sea (same root problem). forge-sea should be closed as duplicate once this is implemented.

## Current State (verified 2026-02-05)
- Disk: 99% used (13G free / 927G total)
- ~/.forge/logs/workers/: **1.4GB** across 14 files
- Top: kilo.log (369MB), lima.log (318MB), echo.log (312MB), juliet.log (238MB)
- No compressed backups exist - rotation never fires
- RotatingWriter exists (forge-2gr) but not compatible with tmux pipe-pane
- compressFile(), TotalSize(), CleanLogs() all exist and work
- foundry logs --clean exists for manual cleanup but nothing runs automatically

## Root Cause Chain
1. internal/worker/lifecycle.go:97 sets cfg.LogFile = logs.WorkerLogPath(w.Name)
2. internal/tmux/session.go:78 runs tmux pipe-pane -t session -o "tee -a logfile"
3. tee -a appends without size limit
4. NATO names reused so same file grows across sessions (alpha.log, bravo.log, etc.)
5. No rotation, no cleanup, no disk warnings

## Technical Approach

### Step 1: Add RotateIfNeeded() to logs package

File: internal/logs/rotate.go (new)

RotateIfNeeded(logPath string, maxSize int64) error:
- Stat the file, return nil if missing or under threshold
- Rename to logPath.YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS
- Compress rotated file in background goroutine (reuse existing compressFile)
- Cleanup old backups beyond limit (keep 5)

cleanupBackups(logPath string, maxBackups int) error:
- Glob for logPath.* rotated files
- Sort by modification time
- Remove oldest beyond maxBackups

### Step 2: Wire into worker lifecycle

File: internal/worker/lifecycle.go - before line 97

Call logs.RotateIfNeeded(logPath, 10*1024*1024) before setting cfg.LogFile.
Warn on stderr if rotation fails (non-fatal).

### Step 3: Add supervisor disk usage warning

File: cmd/foundry/supervisor.go - in health check

Check logs.TotalSize() each cycle. Warn when total exceeds 500MB.
Suggest running foundry logs --clean.

### Step 4: Unit tests

File: internal/logs/rotate_test.go (new)

- Test RotateIfNeeded rotates when file exceeds threshold
- Test RotateIfNeeded no-ops for small files
- Test RotateIfNeeded no-ops for missing files
- Test cleanupBackups removes oldest beyond limit
- Test compressed backup is created

## Existing Infrastructure to Leverage
- compressFile() at internal/logs/logs.go:256 (fully implemented gzip)
- TotalSize() at internal/logs/logs.go:499 (calculates total size)
- CleanLogs() at internal/logs/logs.go:460 (age-based cleanup)
- RotatingWriter at internal/logs/logs.go:73 (patterns to extract from)
- cleanupOldBackups() at internal/logs/logs.go:230 (backup cleanup pattern)

## Files to Create/Modify
| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| internal/logs/rotate.go | New: RotateIfNeeded(), cleanupBackups() |
| internal/logs/rotate_test.go | New: Unit tests |
| internal/worker/lifecycle.go | Call RotateIfNeeded() before line 97 |
| cmd/foundry/supervisor.go | Add disk usage warning to health check |

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Worker logs rotated when exceeding 10MB before new session starts
- [ ] Rotated logs compressed as .gz files
- [ ] Max 5 backups kept per worker name
- [ ] Supervisor warns when total log usage exceeds 500MB
- [ ] Existing foundry logs --clean still works
- [ ] Tests pass: make test
- [ ] Builds cleanly: make build

## Immediate Mitigation
Run manually to free disk space now:
foundry logs --clean --age 1d

## Related Code
- RotatingWriter: internal/logs/logs.go:73-151
- compressFile: internal/logs/logs.go:256-312
- TotalSize: internal/logs/logs.go:499-510
- Worker lifecycle: internal/worker/lifecycle.go:97
- Tmux pipe-pane: internal/tmux/session.go:75-82
- Log paths: internal/logs/logs.go (WorkerLogPath, SessionLogPath)
- Log CLI: cmd/foundry/logs.go
- Existing tests: internal/logs/logs_test.go
- Related task: forge-sea (duplicate, close after this is done)

title: Wire apiErrorTracker.Record() to supervisor error paths
description:
The apiErrorTracker in supervisor state is initialized but Record() is never called. Wire it to: runClaudeHaiku() failures, worker.Start() failures, getSmartDecisions() Haiku call failures. Without this, API error detection is dead code. Follow-up from forge-mcd review.

## Review Feedback (by charlie, Review Leader)

### Status: Changes Requested

### Build & Tests: PASS
Build, tests, go vet all clean.

### What Works Well
- Consistent signature updates: startLeader and assessWithHaiku gain apiTracker param, all 10+ call sites updated
- Nil checks on apiTracker.Record() are defensive and correct
- runClaudeHaiku() failure tracking in assessWithHaiku and getSmartDecisions is semantically correct (these are actual API calls)

### Issues to Fix

#### 1. BUG: worker.Start() failures recorded as API errors (3 sites)
worker.Start() launches a tmux session via forge — this is NOT an API call. Recording it in apiErrorTracker inflates API error counts with unrelated failures (tmux errors, disk errors, etc.). This can trigger API error throttling when the API is fine.

Affected sites:
- assignTasks goroutine (supervisor.go ~line 1908)
- startLeader (supervisor.go ~line 2095)
- executeSmartAction (supervisor.go ~line 4099)

Fix: Remove apiTracker.Record() from these 3 worker.Start() error paths. These should use failureTracker.Record(false) instead (which forge-3bb already adds for the first two). Only keep apiTracker.Record() for actual API calls (runClaudeHaiku failures).

#### 2. DEPENDENCY: Branch forked from task/ddo, not main
This branch includes commit c1ed0f9 from task/ddo which has changes requested. Will need rebase onto main (or merged ddo) before merge.

### Data Structures
```go
// internal/context/learnings.go
type Learning struct {
    ID          string    `json:"id"`
    Summary     string    `json:"summary"`      // One-line summary
    Problem     string    `json:"problem"`      // What went wrong
    Solution    string    `json:"solution"`     // How it was fixed
    Keywords    []string  `json:"keywords"`     // Matching keywords
    Files       []string  `json:"files"`        // Related files
    CreatedAt   time.Time `json:"created_at"`
    SourceTask  string    `json:"source_task"`  // Where this came from
}

type LearningsStore struct {
    Learnings []Learning `json:"learnings"`
    UpdatedAt time.Time  `json:"updated_at"`
}

const MaxLearnings = 50  // Keep most recent 50
```

### Storage Location
```
.forge/
├── context/
│   └── learnings.json   # Auto-maintained by archivist
├── prompts/
│   └── archivist.md     # Updated to write learnings
└── worktrees/
```

### Keyword Matching
```go
// internal/context/match.go
func FindRelevantLearnings(store *LearningsStore, task *kanban.Issue, limit int) []Learning {
    // Extract keywords from task title + description
    taskKeywords := extractKeywords(task.Title, task.Description)
    
    // Score learnings by keyword overlap
    type scored struct {
        learning Learning
        score    int
    }
    var results []scored
    
    for _, l := range store.Learnings {
        overlap := countOverlap(l.Keywords, taskKeywords)
        if overlap > 0 {
            results = append(results, scored{l, overlap})
        }
    }
    
    // Sort by score, take top N
    sort.Slice(results, func(i, j int) bool {
        return results[i].score > results[j].score
    })
    
    var relevant []Learning
    for i := 0; i < limit && i < len(results); i++ {
        relevant = append(relevant, results[i].learning)
    }
    return relevant
}
```

title: Fix: Task show error message truncated
description:
When running 'foundry task show nonexistent-task', the error message is truncated to 'bd show failed:' without showing the actual error.

## Current Behavior
$ foundry task show nonexistent-task
Error: bd show failed: 

## Expected Behavior
$ foundry task show nonexistent-task
Error: task not found: nonexistent-task

## Root Cause
In internal/kanban/store.go:101-115, the Get() function:
1. Runs 'bd show <id> --json'
2. On exit error, checks stderr for "not found" → returns nil, nil
3. If stderr doesn't contain "not found", returns "bd show failed: <stderr>"
4. Problem: stderr is empty for some error cases

The 'bd' command returns empty stderr when task doesn't exist, just non-zero exit code.

## Fix Location
internal/kanban/store.go lines 101-115 in Get() function

## Proposed Fix
```go
func (s *Store) Get(id string) (*Issue, error) {
    cmd := exec.Command("bd", "show", id, "--json")
    cmd.Dir = s.workDir
    out, err := cmd.Output()
    if err != nil {
        if exitErr, ok := err.(*exec.ExitError); ok {
            stderr := string(exitErr.Stderr)
            if strings.Contains(stderr, "not found") || stderr == "" {
                // Not found - return nil without error (caller handles)
                return nil, nil
            }
            return nil, fmt.Errorf("bd show failed: %s", stderr)
        }
        return nil, fmt.Errorf("bd show failed: %w", err)
    }
    // ... rest of function
}
```

Alternative: Improve the error message construction in cmd/foundry/task.go runTaskShow() to always use the "task not found" message when issue is nil.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] 'foundry task show nonexistent' shows "task not found: nonexistent"
- [ ] Existing task show still works correctly
- [ ] Add test case for nonexistent task
- [ ] Compare output matches 'foundry worker status nonexistent' pattern

## Dependencies
None - simple fix in error handling.

title: Add notification webhooks for supervisor events
description:
Allow users to configure webhook endpoints for supervisor events.

## Event Types
1. task_completed - Task moved to done
2. task_failed - Task failed/blocked
3. worker_started - Worker session began
4. worker_stopped - Worker session ended
5. worker_error - Worker encountered error
6. leader_launched - Leader agent started
7. deployment_triggered - Deploy leader activated
8. build_failed - CI/CD failure detected

## Configuration

**Location**: .foundry/webhooks.yaml

```yaml
webhooks:
  - name: slack-notifications
    url: https://hooks.slack.com/services/xxx
    events:
      - task_completed
      - worker_error
    filters:
      priority: [high, critical]
    retry:
      max_attempts: 3
      backoff_seconds: 5

  - name: discord-alerts
    url: https://discord.com/api/webhooks/xxx
    events:
      - deployment_triggered
      - build_failed
```

### New Package: internal/webhooks/
- webhook.go - Types and config loading
- dispatcher.go - Event dispatch with retry
- templates.go - Payload templates per event

1. Config loading first (enables testing webhook format)
2. Dispatcher with retry (core functionality)
3. Hook into worker lifecycle (easiest integration point)
